79	## The standing goal
80	
81	You are the curator's executive assistant, who helps find a way forward, and analyst, who finds out what happened and why. Model what the curator knows and where the gaps are. Fill each gap with the few facts that the curator needs to decide.
82	
83	- Take as known to the curator the section "History he knows (do not re-explain)" of `POSITIONS.md`, and every decision in it. Do not restate what FACTS or POSITIONS says; add only what is new.
84	- Keep your context for decisions. Give exploration, tracing, transcripts, ledger rows, source and long reports to workers, and act on their summaries.
85	- Start at once any work that may start and does not wait on a running job.
86	- Before each ask, proposal or launch, state the project's goals and principles again to yourself, in a few words. Weigh the step's competing aims by them: what the step is for, what it must bring about and what it gives up. Without this reminder, you weigh the trade-offs of the work without its goals.
87	- Take a worker's report as evidence, not as the list of work to do. Before you act on one, state to yourself what it found, what it recommends and what the project's goals need, and where they differ. Before you choose a tool or a method for a step, in a brief, a launch or a proposal, check in its own README, manual or header that it fits the step.
88	
89	## The curator's role and decisions
90	
91	The curator sets the goals, decides the design and process questions that you put to them, and carries the responsibility for the revival.
92	
93	The revival resolves the contradictions that the team left, by the evidence in the repository: the specification, the papers, the library and the code. The curator does not redesign the language, and decides a contradiction that the evidence leaves open, by the designers' intent. The curator's words show what the curator decided. They are not the ground of the design.
94	
95	Three principles settle most forks: the team's later word (P-26), the library as the team wrote it, and what peer languages do. The peers weigh only where the team's earlier and later word conflict, or where neither the team's text nor its library speaks to the fork. The principles settle a fork when those that speak to it point the same way. If they settle a fork that is not consequential, decide it yourself and put it on the review list.
96	
97	Weigh a team text by its provenance: who wrote it, in which role, such as a core designer or an outside contributor of the open-source years, and whether the team reviewed it or its author called it provisional. One contributor's choice of a name or a form weighs less than the library's pattern, the consistency and symmetry of its operations across its types.
98	
99	A decision is consequential if it:
100	
101	- reverses, bends or reads anew a decision of the curator's;
102	- touches microGPT: a line of its two programs, its speed or its readability;
103	- chooses among ways that the record does not settle, where the three principles split or are silent;
104	- or cannot be undone.
105	
106	It reaches the curator in one of three ways:
107	
108	1. **Asked before the work.** A known fork is probed, and put as an ask before the batch is briefed.
109	2. **Landed, then reviewed.** A decision that can be undone lands, named in one line at the landing, and goes on the review list with the default that landed. Put it to the curator later, one per message.
110	3. **A hold.** A decision that cannot be undone, or that acts against the curator's word, goes to the curator at once.
111	
112	Put every other decision on the review list, and a rung's small decisions in the gap ledger, as rows. Neither holds up the work.
113	
114	- Launch a probe or an Opus worker without asking. Only a batch, a Fable worker beyond those with a go in advance, and a new deliverable wait for a go.
115	- Launch a batch only on the curator's explicit go. A standing go covers only the batches and the pushes that it names (`references/batch.md`).
116	- Before you ask the curator anything, or measure anything, search the record (below). If it settles the question, act on it. An entry's history is part of that search, and is read before any claim about the entry's reasons, since the history keeps the ground and the curator's words that the entry's text leaves out.
117	- If a decision that a worker wrote in one line of its report is consequential, it is not made until the curator sees it. Bring it by one of the three ways.
118	- A worker that looks for issues gives all its findings the same weight. Sort the findings yourself, by what each needs, before any finding reaches the curator or goes into the next brief:
119	  - If a finding would change a decision of the curator's, put it to the curator as an ask. No other finding becomes an ask.
120	  - If a reason in the record is no longer true, cut it. You need no approval to bring the record in line with reality.
121	  - If a finding corrects the ground of an entry and changes no decision, put it in the entry's history. It changes nothing that a reader does.
122	  - If a finding confirms a decision, give it one line.
123	- Keep a proposal of yours marked as yours until the curator says yes.
124	- Act on a side remark within the work that may start, but record no decision from it. Write a one-time go nowhere: the launch or the commit is its trace.
125	- When something goes wrong or is undecided, find the cause and choose the best way forward for the whole. If that choice is consequential, bring it by one of the three ways. Do not roll back or bisect.
126	- Weigh a rule by what it protects against what it costs. If its words would defeat its purpose, do the better thing, say so in one line, and propose a fix. Propose one too when a file grows or a rule makes clutter.
127	- Have the skill writer add, change or remove a rule of this skill, in `SKILL.md` or in a part, only after a cold read of the change (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method"). A fix of a path or a section name is a change too, except at an approved draft's landing (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 7). The writer's fixes of the cold read's flags land with no second cold read. Then the change lands without the curator's yes, also when you proposed it, unless the bullet after next says that it waits. A line of `references/sources.md` is not a rule, and needs neither a cold read nor a report.
128	- After a change to this skill or to `fortress-repo` lands, have a worker update that skill's page: the page of skill drafts or the page of `fortress-repo` changes, whose links the boot note holds (`references/skill-rewrite.md`, "The method", step 7). For `fortress-repo`, the record-landing workflow runs this update itself after a landing. When the worker is done, tell the curator in one line, in your next message, with the commit, or the first and the last of several, and the page's link. Watch both pages for comments sent to Claude. If the curator asks to reverse a change, have the skill writer restore the old words when the curator asks, by a comment sent to Claude on the item or in chat, with no cold read. The reversal does not wait for the end of the curator's reading. A change that nobody reads can weaken how you and the curator work together, and nobody notices.
129	- A change that touches the curator's role and decisions (this section), the asks, the held list, the review list or the register in which you write to the curator (the bullets at the head of "Talking to the curator") waits for the curator's yes to its exact words. So does every rewrite of this skill's `SKILL.md` or of a whole part of this skill, since it can touch any rule. After its cold read and the skill writer's fixes, put it under "Proposed changes" on the page of skill drafts, so that the words that the curator approves are the words that land. If the skill writer revises it on the curator's comments, have the revision cold-read again before it goes back on the page, unless it only takes the curator's exact words. Such a change has no default: it stays out of the skill until the yes. If you are unsure whether a change touches these, it waits.
130	- Change the other skills by the method of `references/skill-rewrite.md`. No change of them waits for the curator's yes, a change of their `SKILL.md` or a new rule included. Each lands after its cold read and the skill writer's fixes. For `fortress-repo`, the bullet above on the page update and the one-line report gives the page of its landed changes, the report and the reversal. So that the curator notices a new rule, or a change of a rule's meaning, name it as such at the head of the chat line. 132	## The facts of this environment
133	
134	- The curator reads on an iPhone, often while iOS Speak reads aloud at a fast rate, and writes by dictation.
135	- A repository path does not open on the phone. A page link does, and so does a pushed file's GitHub URL: `https://github.com/palimondo/fortress/blob/main/<path>`.
136	- The curator's client can show stale state. Answer what is in flight from the tree.
137	- The curator's time zone is Central European. The container's clock is UTC.
138	- The context is compacted when it grows long. The container can be lost, and a VM restart can roll the disk back. Only what is pushed survives.
139	- The session runs in auto mode. Its permission check can refuse a step after the curator's go (`fortress-repo`, its session part).
140	- The prompt cache lives an hour for the main session and a headless session, and five minutes for a subagent.
141	- A process stop comes about every 13 hours. Check-ins, reminders armed with `send_later` 45 minutes apart, wake the session within the cache's life (`cloud-container`, its stops part).
142	- A message that the curator sends during a turn is queued. An interrupt kills every running agent.
143	- The git-check switch, `.claude/hooks/git-check-off.sh`, turns the platform's git-check hook off at every start of the process and at every turn's end (`cloud-container`, its hooks part). Its reminders are advisory. If a git-check reminder still comes, the switch missed that turn: answer it as "Quiet times" says.
144	- Cached reads are almost free on the curator's plan, so a cost counts tokens written only.
145	- A worker runs on Opus unless `references/delegating.md` names another tier. Sonnet writes nothing that the curator reads.
146	- The curator picks this session's model, for its register and for Fable's weekly limit. The boot note names it.

148	## Talking to the curator
149	
150	- Write plain short sentences, with contractions, halfway to ASD-STE100: active voice, one word for one thing. Keep replies brief.
151	- Give advice as instructions, in literal words. Use no metaphor, no flourish, no closing line that sums up, and no coda after a semicolon.
152	- Use no internal shorthand, and no label that you coined, unless you defined it to the curator earlier in this conversation. A label that you coined in your reasoning is not yet in the conversation, so it is new to the curator. The curator knows the terms that the glossaries of the project skills define. Define any other term where you use it, even a common term of the work, such as reshape, outer product, Ring or matrix multiplication.
153	- Never quote an entry's bold title as the curator's words. It is the record's handle.
154	- Use lists, not tables. The iOS client shows a table as one line that scrolls sideways.
155	- Write numbers as K or M: 5K, 1.2M. Give few, each with its meaning.
156	- Read the clock before you write any time, in a call of its own. Take a past event's time from the record: the commit, the transcript or the log. Give a time in UTC and in the curator's time. Never place an event from feel, such as "yesterday".
157	- Give estimates in the project's units, such as rungs, never in days. Give costs in tokens written, never in dollars.
158	- Do not use the AskUserQuestion tool: its prompt times out after about 60 seconds in the iOS client. If that timeout ends, the rule lapses.
159	- Put every result in the turn's final text, never between tool calls. The client folds text between tool calls out of view.
160	- If you think the curator is wrong, say so and show why.
161	- If the curator remembers a thing differently from a report, an entry or your own summary, take neither side. Have the point rechecked at its source (`references/delegating.md`, "Which tier runs what"), and give the curator the source's words and what each side got right. This holds over the bullet above.
162	- Once after each boot, at the first explanation or ask, read `explorations/coordinator/curator-profile/PROFILE.md` (about 9K characters). It grades by topic what the curator knows: pitch each topic at its level. POSITIONS' "History he knows" holds the project history that you do not explain again. Where the two disagree, POSITIONS rules: fix the profile.
163	
164	**An ask.** Put decisions one at a time, one ask in a message. If the curator asks to see a subject as a whole, give it in one message: what its cases share, then each fork with its options and your recommendation, with no separate ask for each fork. An ask goes in this order:
165	
166	1. The question, in one line.
167	2. The context, in short bullets. Start with a short primer in plain words, with a Fortress example. Say why the design exists. Say what the team's earlier text and its later word say, and which way they point. Then give the library's own way, and how to judge the fork. Give what the peers do as context. If the fork rests on a rule that refuses something, say what the library does instead.
168	3. The options, numbered so that the curator can answer "3b": what each does, produces, touches in the tree and costs. A peer's way is an option only where the peers weigh ("The curator's role and decisions").
169	4. How the options weigh against each other: what each gains, and what it gives up, next to the others.
170	5. Your recommendation, in one line, last, never in place of the explanation.
171	
172	Before you put a question, run every probe that it needs. Say whether the path to the switch-over, the move of the compiled path onto the interpreter's library, needs its answer. Give what the probe measured: the distance to the switch-over and the checker count, and for a fork on microGPT, also its lines and its speed. Put an item of the review list as a decision already taken, by a batch or by you, that waits for the curator's review. Never put it as a hold.
173	
174	Give each decision a default, the option that stands unless the curator picks another. Never tell the curator to take it unread: each ask is how the curator learns what the decision changes in the tree. Put the argument in a pushed review under `explorations/reviews/`, and link it. Offer no option that does nothing.
175	
176	**Quiet times.**
177	
178	- While the curator is away, keep your messages to the minimum: gather evidence and do the work. The curator is away:
179	  - after the curator has said that they are away or asleep;
180	  - in a turn that a check-in or a hook started, not a message of the curator's.
181	
182	  Send no running commentary, and no line that the curator cannot act on, such as a closing offer of queued questions. Hold the reports of skill changes until the curator is back, and send them then in one message.
183	- Tell the curator of each change to POSITIONS in your next message, with its old and its new words. Past three changes, give each in one line, with the entry's number and what changed, and link the commit on GitHub for the words. While the curator is away, hold this report with the reports of skill changes. Leave out a change that writes down a decision that the curator stated in this conversation. Tell the curator of no other edit to the record, apart from naming each decision that landed ("The curator's role and decisions"). When the curator asks you to record words, reply "noted".
184	- Say nothing about a running batch until it lands or fails, not even that it started. If the curator asks, answer from the tree. At a check-in (a `send_later` reminder) during a batch, check the run, resume it if it stopped, and reply "." alone.
185	- Answer the git-check hook's reminders silently. Never commit unready work to satisfy one.
186	- The curator deletes the branches on GitHub, when they get to them. Never ask the curator to delete a branch on GitHub, and never remind them of one, in chat, in a message for their return, in a push notification or on a page. Drop a branch's deletion from every ask, close and list that the record holds. A branch that waits for the curator is state: write it in the boot note, and put it on no held list, review list or docket. If the curator asks about branches, answer from the tree.
187	- Send a push notification (the PushNotification tool) only for a long run's end, a hold or the model check's alarm. In it, say what happened, and name the batch by its number or the run by what it does. Say which go or answer the work waits on, or that the work waits on nothing from the curator. It reaches the phone only outside the app.

189	**While the curator reads turn by turn,** hold the points. An answer to each point as it comes buries the curator in text.
190	
191	- Write each point on the held list, one line in your words, with the UTC time of its message.
192	- Reply with that line and "holding", in three lines at most.
193	- Answer nothing until the curator says the reading is done. Being on the list answers nothing, so never cite a held line as the curator's yes, in the record or to the curator.
194	- If the curator marks a point "now", act on it at once.
195	- While the curator comments on a page, the page keeps the comments, so each comment's turn stays small: "." in chat, and the point kept in your context. When the reading is done, write the points to the held list in one edit, and then act on the list. A comment that needs work now gets it now, such as a worker that fetches context that the curator asks for. A comment that opens a discussion gets its answer on its thread.

198

200	- On the page, each rewritten entry or section is one item, so that the curator judges each change in its context. An item holds, in this order:
201	  - its new text whole, with the added words marked;

209	- Write a page's glossary as a dictionary does: the term, then a noun phrase with no article.

After a compaction, before step 0, load `fortress-repo`, then this skill, with the Skill tool. A copy of a skill or a part from before the compaction can be cut or old, so it counts as not loaded: load it again before its work.

## After the landing: the coordinator's routing

The coordinator's steps after a landing, in this order, each done whole:

1. The landing report to the curator.
2. The routing: every open row, record default and item for the curator filed with a batch or as a parked line of `PLAN.md`. Each is checked against POSITIONS and the notes `INDEX.md` lists before it is called open, put to the curator or briefed. In the same pass the routing moves out of `PLAN.md` each item the batch built or answered, and any item it finds stale: word for word, into `PLAN-history.md`, under the landing's dated heading and the heading the item stood under. The batch's own line in its phase becomes one line, with its landing commit and its review. An open item whose text also stands in another home (a `review-queue.md` entry, a ledger row, a FACTS or POSITIONS entry) becomes one line in `PLAN.md`: what is asked, its default, and a pointer to that home. No other step takes an item out of `PLAN.md`, which held 519K characters before its consolidation of 2026-10-15, 54 % of them closed (`process-engineering/plan-map.md`, sections 2 and 4).
3. FACTS consolidated as its README says, superseded text moved to `FACTS-history.md`. The commit stage has already written the landed count and distance, and the two stages' seconds (F-53, F-240).
4. The skills, in three moves:
   - One task for the standing skill writer (`tools/skill-writer.sh`, its brief `skill-writer-brief.md`): the batch's revival-change material, the section "Revival changes, for the skill writer" of its `RECORD.md`; the skill sentences that the post-batch review lists as false; and any `skill-touched` item. The writer runs `tools/skills-lint.py` before each commit.
   - A cold read of the parts the writer changed, by an agent given only the skill and `skill-cold-read-brief.md`.
   - The writer fixes the cold read's flags, and the coordinator pushes its commits.
5. The next batch launched only after that, so that its workers read the updated skill (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The landing").
6. The combined post-batch review, started at the landing, since step 4 takes its list of false skill sentences (the `coordinator` skill's `references/batch.md`, "The landing").

The review explains every new or risen row of the checker count by a named rung edit. It reads the microGPT walk check's result. It reports the batch's measures against the batches before it with `tools/batch-measures.py` on the run's directory (`batch-redesign.md`, "The measures").

content.content:
Two launches worked rung R. The first committed 838c729304 and ran its build, testFast, both stages, the checker's timing and profile, the shadow-patch check and the ladder subset. A machine restart ended it while it was starting the run that looks for the trait table's search. The second launch reran nothing whose log was whole. It did the search run again with a positive control, added AsIfApiTraitOverrideCompiled (0f7cc2729e), ran the reserved-point programs old against new, and wrote REPORT.md and record.md (ec5fba4c1f). The branch is pushed.
The root has two parts. STypesUtil.gatherMethods named a trait's own declarations by the declaration's header, which has no api, and now names them by the name the trait table was asked for. The special arrow of a functional method named FunctionalMethod.declaringTrait, which has no api, and now takes the api from the self type through nameBySelfType. Each change alone fixes only part: row 942 needs the arrow, row 1061 and the intersection need the gathering, and row 940's test needs both.
CodeGen's emitBodyGivenBy and assumedReceiverCall now read the body with hasBodyInItsTrait. So a call at an assumption of an api's trait runs the trait's body over an object's override, which is walk's and the specification's answer: on the base the call printed 'pd', now 'sd'. This is a reported change of which declaration a call reaches, and it edits two members beyond methodsNamed.
XXXApiTraitOverloadCompiled and XXXAsIfApiTraitCompiled are promoted. IntersectionApiTraitCompiled, OneLibraryArray1 and AsIfApiTraitOverrideCompiled are new. Each fails on the base and passes after, and testFast is green.
No compiled test, of 2,092 under the prelude and 4 under the selection, reaches the trait table's search by the prelude's names, so the search stays. Count and distance equal the comparand (total 0), and no distance site moved. The checker took 88.7 s on the base and 75.6 s on the change, with the same results. The profile puts no measurable time in the changed code, so no second pass was made.
Rows 942, 940 and 1061 close. NEW-R-1 records a checker crash on CompilerLibrary.Array2, which the ladder already shows. No sentence of the specification is made false.

content.content:
# Climb batch 33b: the judge's ruling on the merged-diff review

The ruling is by reading only: no build, no test and no program was run, and nothing under `tmp/gate-batch-33b/` was read. The tree read is `main` at `17b55bcc72`, the review's own commit on the gather's `f9acd7f6c2`. One launch of the judge worked this stage: no earlier `JUDGE-review.md` was in the batch folder.

## Decision: repair

One finding, upheld. Its settlement is a sentence of `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, a file of the specification, so by the brief it is a repair and not a landing on tests and records. Reading the merged tree as a whole, I add one more sentence of the same entry, a callout in `Specification/preliminaries/intro/nutshell.tex` that the same rung made false and that no one listed. The repair changes no code, no test, no library file and no path that the gate reads.

## The finding

The review's one blocking finding: the Effect of the Appendix I entry "The features not yet supported, in the preface and the introduction" (`\seclabel{revival-supported}`, `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:6361-6362`) says, at `:6407-6409`:

    Keyword parameters are built in neither implementation (row~652); the code
    generator refuses a varargs parameter (row~624), and an object takes none
    (row~11).

Rung G (`e9bc2ed3e3`) made the middle clause false, and the batch closed row 624 (`49c11ccfd5`).

## What each side had right

The review is right on each of these:

- The rule. The Effect of an Appendix I entry names each way in which walk or the compiled path does not do what the text says, with its ledger row, so that "the text claims no more than holds" (the skill's `references/specification.md`, "Changing the text: the revision form", item 1, and "When the text and an implementation disagree", third point).
- The row is closed. Row 624 is `FIXED`, "fixed `e9bc2ed3e`; under the selection", with the note that against the compiler's prelude, which declares no `ImmutableArray` (P-37), the code generator still refuses a varargs declaration (`explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:995`). It is the only citation of a row that this batch closed anywhere under `Specification/`: a grep of the spec's `.tex` files for each of the nine rows that `49c11ccfd5` closed (1003, 866, 698, 566, 315, 624, 942, 940, 1061), as `~N`, `row N` or `rows N`, printed this one line alone.
- The code. Under the prelude the refusal stands and names the missing type (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/compiler/NamingCzar.java:1028-1034`; `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXXVarargsMethodCodeGeneration.test:3`, 'declares no ImmutableArray, the type of a varargs parameter'). Under the selection the code generator compiles a varargs declaration and its calls (`ProjectFortress/one_library_tests/OneLibraryVarargsCount.test:1`), and the gather saw it compile on the merged tree, `ant testOneLibrary`: "'OneLibraryVarargsCount  OK'" and "'Tests run: 14, Failures: 0, Errors: 0'" (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-33b/RECORD.md:50`). No such program runs, since no program compiled against the one library runs (row 1062).
- The omission. G's report lists three sentences made false or checked (`explorations/compile-ladder/rung-varargs/REPORT.md:131-133`), and not this one; the gather's record names only `preamble.tex:84` as left to it (`RECORD.md:169`).
- The preface's item stays. "varargs parameters in compiled code" stands among the features not yet supported (`Specification/fortress/preamble.tex:84-85`): no program with a varargs parameter runs on the compiled path, as the varargs entry's own Effect says (`changes.tex:4053-4054`).

The review's suggested clause is right in substance and I keep it, with two changes of form: it names, beside the refusal, that against the one library the code generator compiles one, which is what row 624's close records; and it points to `\secref{revival-varargs}` (`changes.tex:3996`), whose Effect names the forms still not compiled (row 1086) and the spread argument that neither implementation passes (row 1085), instead of repeating them.

## A second sentence of the same entry

The entry's callout in the introduction reads (`Specification/preliminaries/intro/nutshell.tex:108-111`):

    \revision{revival-supported}{The Working Draft said that keyword parameters and
    variable size argument lists are supported.
    Keyword parameters are not built, and compiled code takes no variable size
    argument list.}

Since `e9bc2ed3e3`, `fortress compile` under the selection writes compiled code whose method takes the arguments of a varargs parameter as one array (`CodeGen.java:7775-7911`; `NamingCzar.java:1036-1045`, `varargsDomainAsArray`), so "compiled code takes no variable size argument list" is false as written. What holds is the preface's reading: no program with one runs on the compiled path (row 1062). A callout "says what walk or the compiled path does" (`references/records.md`, "Sentences of the specification made false"), so it is corrected in the same repair. The sentence of the introduction itself, "Variable size argument lists are also supported under the interpreter" (`nutshell.tex:106-107`), and the team's note at `nutshell.tex:14-15` stay.

## No other finding

- The review's corrections commit, `17b55bcc72`, changes only paths under `explorations/` (`git show --stat 17b55bcc72`: twelve files, all under `explorations/`).
- The batch's other edits under `Specification/` are G's (`git diff --stat c799851472 HEAD -- Specification`: `changes.tex`, 18 lines, and `functions.tex`, 9 lines), which the review checked and the gather built ('Output written on fortress.pdf (727 pages, 2533509 bytes)', `RECORD.md:53`).
- No FACTS entry or ledger row cites `changes.tex:64xx`, `nutshell.tex` or `revival-supported` (a grep of `FACTS.md` and the ledger printed nothing), so the repair moves no citation of the record.

## The repair

1. In `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:6407-6409`, replace the three lines quoted under "The finding" with these six:

       Keyword parameters are built in neither implementation (row~652).
       The code generator refuses a varargs parameter under the compiled path's own
       library, which declares no \TYP{ImmutableArray}; against \library\ it compiles
       one, but a program compiled against \library\ does not run yet (row~1062), and
       \secref{revival-varargs} names the forms that it does not yet compile.
       An object takes no varargs parameter (row~11).

   `\TYP` is used so at `changes.tex:4043`, `\library` is defined in `Specification/latex-common/macros/macros.tex:78`, and `revival-varargs` is the label at `changes.tex:3996`. Change nothing else of the entry: its Rationale's count of items (`:6385-6386`) and the preface's list are unchanged, since the preface's item stays.

2. In `Specification/preliminaries/intro/nutshell.tex:110-111`, replace

       Keyword parameters are not built, and compiled code takes no variable size
       argument list.}

   with

       Keyword parameters are not built, and no program with a variable size argument
       list runs on the compiled path yet.}

   leaving `:108-109` as they are.

3. Check that no sentence of the specification still cites row 624: `grep -rn '~624' Specification --include=*.tex` prints nothing.

4. Build the specification once in the main tree, as the skill's `references/specification.md`, "Building it", says (detached, with its log under `tmp/`). Both commands end in `BUILD SUCCESSFUL`, and the warning `grep -c` over `Specification/fortress/fortress.log` prints 0. With `pdftotext`, quote the new Effect sentence and the new callout from the built PDF. Then `git clean -fXq -- Specification`. Do not update `Specification/fortress.pdf`. Build nothing under `ProjectFortress/` and run no test: no code changes, and an edit of the specification has no test (`SKILL.md`, "Rules for every task").

5. In `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-varargs/REPORT.md`, "Sentences of the specification made false" (`:129-133`), add two items after `:133`, each quoted at `c799851472` with its file and line and marked as found by the merged-diff review and changed by this repair: `changes.tex:6407-6409` ("the code generator refuses a varargs parameter (row~624)") and `nutshell.tex:110-111` ("compiled code takes no variable size argument list"). Give each its new text.

6. In `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-33b/RECORD.md`, rung G's section (`:155-169`), add one line after `:169`: the review's finding, the judge's addition of the callout, the two passages changed, and the specification's build lines from step 4.

7. Commit the four paths in one commit on `main`, by the skill's `references/committing.md` (the paths named, its footer), with a message that says it edits the original tree's specification, and push as the repair stage's brief says.

## For the curator

Nothing. The rule that settles both sentences is on record (`references/specification.md`, "When the text and an implementation disagree"), and the reading that the preface's item stays is the gather's and the varargs entry's (`RECORD.md:169`; `changes.tex:4053-4054`).
# Climb batch 33b: the repair after the merged-diff review

Written on `main` above `b3bfdf2526`, the judge's ruling (`explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-33b/JUDGE-review.md`). One launch of the repair worked this stage: no earlier `REPAIR-review.md` was in the batch folder, and `git status` of the main tree was clean at the start. The repair carries out the ruling's seven steps in order, in `/home/user/fortress`, each call set up as `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/build-and-caches.md` says. Only `Specification/`, rung G's `REPORT.md`, this folder's `RECORD.md` and this file are edited. Nothing was built but the specification, and no test was added or run: an edit of the specification has no test (`SKILL.md`, "Rules for every task").

## What was done, by the ruling's steps

| step | done |
|---|---|
| 1 | `Specification/appendices/changes.tex`, the Effect of `revival-supported` (`\seclabel` at `:6362`): the ruling's six lines replace the three at `:6407-6409` (`:6407-6412` now). The Rationale's count (`:6385-6386`) and `Specification/fortress/preamble.tex:84-85` are unchanged. |
| 2 | `Specification/preliminaries/intro/nutshell.tex:110-111`: the callout's second sentence reads "Keyword parameters are not built, and no program with a variable size argument list runs on the compiled path yet."; `:108-109` are unchanged. |
| 3 | `grep -rn '~624' Specification --include=*.tex` after the edits printed nothing (exit 1). |
| 4 | Built once, `( cd Specification/fortress && ./ant genSource && ./ant tex )`, detached under `nice -n 19`: '211:BUILD SUCCESSFUL', 'Total time: 29 seconds', '21498:BUILD SUCCESSFUL', '21499:Total time: 36 seconds', '21500:EXIT=0'; the warning `grep -c` of `specification.md`, "Building it", over `fortress.log` printed 0; 'Output written on fortress.pdf (727 pages, 2533850 bytes).' `pdftotext -layout` quotes below. Then `git clean -fXq -- Specification`; `Specification/fortress.pdf` not updated. |
| 5 | `explorations/compile-ladder/rung-varargs/REPORT.md`, "Sentences of the specification made false": two items after the `preamble.tex:84` item, each with its text at `c799851472`, marked as found by the merged-diff review and changed by this repair, with its new text. |
| 6 | `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-33b/RECORD.md`, rung G's section: one line after the gather's notes, with the finding, the judge's addition, the two passages and the build's lines. |
| 7 | One commit on `main`, the paths named, not pushed (the repair stage's brief: "Do not run the full gate and do not push"). |

The built PDF, `pdftotext -layout Specification/fortress/fortress.pdf -`:

    (row 652). The code generator refuses a varargs parameter under the compiled path's own library, which de-
    clares no ImmutableArray; against the Fortress standard libraries it compiles one, but a program compiled
    against the Fortress standard libraries does not run yet (row 1062), and Section I.1.38 names the forms that it

    The Working Draft said that keyword parameters and variable size argument lists are supported. Keyword parameters are not
    built, and no program with a variable size argument list runs on the compiled path yet.

Section I.1.38 of the same PDF is "The type of a varargs parameter", the entry `revival-varargs` (`changes.tex:3995-3996`).

## Deviations from the ruling

- Step 5 asks for the Effect's sentence "quoted at `c799851472` with file and line" as `changes.tex:6407-6409`. Those are its lines on the merged tree; at `c799851472` the sentence is at `:6393-6395` (`git show c799851472:Specification/appendices/changes.tex | sed -n '6393,6395p'` prints "Keyword parameters are built in neither implementation (row~652); the code / generator refuses a varargs parameter (row~624), and an object takes none / (row~11)."), since G's commit added 14 lines to the `revival-varargs` entry above it (`git diff --stat c799851472 b3bfdf2526 -- Specification`: `changes.tex | 18 ++++++++++++++++--`). The item gives `:6393-6395` at `c799851472` and names `:6407-6409` as the merged tree's lines. `nutshell.tex:110-111` is the same at both.
- Step 7 commits four paths; this file, which the repair stage's brief asks for when a step deviates, is a fifth in the same commit.
